PART-TIME Remote Administrative Scheduler | 20–30 Hours/Week

100% Remote | Monday–Friday | $18.50–$20.00/hour, based on experience

Paragon Planners is looking for a professional, dependable, and highly organized Administrative Scheduler to join our remote team.

In this role, you’ll support professionals in the financial services industry by managing schedules, connecting with clients, and helping keep their day-to-day operations organized and running smoothly.

This position offers 20–30 hours per week, with work taking place during regular Monday - Friday business hours. It’s a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working with people, takes pride in staying organized, and is looking for meaningful professional work without a traditional 40-hour schedule.

What You’ll Do

As an Administrative Scheduler, you’ll build relationships with the professionals you support while helping them stay connected with their clients.

Your responsibilities will include:

• 

Making outbound calls to schedule and confirm appointments

• 

Communicating professionally with clients by phone and email

• 

Managing calendars and coordinating schedules

• 

Entering and maintaining accurate information in client databases

• 

Following established processes and client-specific instructions

• 

Providing dependable administrative support throughout the workweek

This role is a good fit for someone who is personable, comfortable on the phone, detail-oriented, and enjoys being the person who keeps things organized behind the scenes.

Schedule & Availability

Because our Administrative Schedulers support clients throughout the business day, consistent Monday–Friday availability is required.

• 

Availability is needed during standard business hours, generally 8:30 AM–5:00 PM in the client’s time zone

• 

Both morning and afternoon availability are required throughout the week

• 

Working hours may not fall into one continuous block each day

• 

Schedules are based on the needs of the clients you support

• 

Initial hours may build gradually as you complete onboarding and are assigned to clients

This position is designed for candidates specifically seeking part-time work. If you are seeking a traditional 40-hour workweek or full-time employment, this position will not be the right fit.

Training & Onboarding

We provide training and support to help new employees learn our systems, processes, and the expectations of the role.

New employees should plan for approximately 8–12 hours of training per week during the initial training period. As you progress through onboarding, you may begin working with clients while continuing to complete your training.

Client assignments are based on current business needs and finding the right match between employees and the professionals they support, so candidates should be comfortable with a gradual ramp-up in hours.

What We’re Looking For

Successful candidates are typically:

• 

Warm, polished, and professional communicators

• 

Comfortable speaking with clients by phone

• 

Highly organized and detail-oriented

• 

Dependable and responsive

• 

Able to work independently and manage their time effectively

• 

Comfortable following detailed instructions and adapting to different client preferences

• 

Comfortable learning new technology

• 

Experienced in administrative support, scheduling, customer service, or another client-facing role

• 

Interested in a long-term professional opportunity

Previous remote-work experience is helpful, but not required.

Location Requirements

We are currently only hiring in the following states: AL, AZ, FL, GA, ID, KY, LA, MI, MO, NC, OH, OR, SC, TN, TX, UT & WY.

Applicants must reside in one of the states listed above to be considered.

We do not hire outside of the United States.

Home Office & Technology Requirements

Because this is a fully remote position, employees must have:

• 

A quiet, professional home-office environment suitable for client calls

• 

Reliable high-speed internet

• 

A Windows 11 computer

• 

The ability to participate in video meetings and training

Macs, iPads, Chromebooks, and virtual machines are not compatible with the technology requirements of this position.

Background Screening

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of required background screening. Due to the nature of our work within the financial services industry, our screening process is comprehensive and may include multiple background checks.

Compensation

Starting pay: $18.50–$20.00 per hour, based on relevant experience.

Employees are eligible for a compensation review after six months, with opportunities for continued increases as they gain experience and tenure with Paragon Planners.

About Paragon Planners

Paragon Planners provides administrative and scheduling support to professionals in the financial services industry. Our remote team helps clients manage their schedules, stay connected with their customers, and keep important day-to-day details moving.

We value professionalism, dependability, strong communication, and people who genuinely enjoy helping others.

Ready to Apply?

If you enjoy working with people, love keeping things organized, and are looking for a professional remote role with weekday hours, we’d love to hear from you.

Please follow all application instructions carefully. Incomplete or incorrectly submitted applications will not be considered.

Paragon Planners is an equal opportunity employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/paragon-planners-part-time-remote-administrative-scheduler

About the Role

At Databricks Information Technology, we are a product-led organisation transforming the way we work, from how easy it is to use our IT services to the applications we develop to help us scale seamlessly amid incredible growth.

As an IT Software Engineer (Infrastructure), you will be a core technical contributor on the IT CorpEng Infrastructure team, owning and driving the evolution of our core infrastructure and observability platforms. This role requires a strong software engineering mindset, deep technical breadth across SRE and infrastructure worlds, and the ability to deliver high-quality, scalable solutions for currently "immature" system problems. You will be responsible for building resilient, scalable, and automated infrastructure that empowers our development teams. As a member of the team, you will bridge the gap between software engineering and systems architecture, ensuring our AWS environment is cost-optimised, secure, and highly available.

The impact you will have:

  • Automate: Develop and deploy production-grade infrastructure on cloud platforms (AWS preferred) using Infrastructure as Code tools like Terraform or Pulumi.
  • Orchestration: Deploy, manage, and scale containerised workloads using Kubernetes (EKS/AKS), focusing on security, reliability, and resource efficiency.
  • CI/CD Excellence: Build and maintain robust deployment pipelines using GitHub Actions, including both cloud-hosted and self-hosted runners for specialised build requirements.
  • Drive "Observable by Default" Frameworks: Implement infrastructure standards to ensure new internal applications are secure, with logging, metrics, and tracing configured out of the box.
  • Tooling, Scripting & AI: Build internal CLI tools, AI-assisted workflows, and automation scripts to streamline developer workflows and reduce manual toil.
  • Partner Cross-Functionally: Collaborate with Security, Engineering, Infrastructure, and Support teams to execute technical projects aligned with business outcomes.
  • Document & Knowledge Share: Participate in peer code reviews, maintain operational playbooks/failure triage guides, and help onboard team members onto platforms you maintain.

What we look for:

  • Software Engineering Expertise: 3–5 years of hands-on software engineering experience, with strong proficiency in Python for scripting, automation, and tooling (required).
  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Solid working knowledge of Terraform (modules, state management) or Pulumi (preferred).
  • Cloud & Containerization: Hands-on experience building and supporting production workloads in AWS (or Azure/GCP), along with Kubernetes and Docker fundamentals.
  • CI/CD & Automation: Practical experience designing, maintaining, and troubleshooting pipelines using GitHub Actions or similar modern CI/CD tools.
  • Observability Foundations: Practical understanding of observability pillars (logging, metrics, tracing) and hands-on experience integrating tools such as Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana.
  • Independent Execution: Proven ability to own end-to-end tasks with guidance from Tech Leads, breaking down broader technical goals into actionable technical solutions.

fcbe6bafd61d7005.description: ## About Metaforms Metaforms is a vertically integrated AI SaaS platform for market research agencies around the world. The platform helps agencies improve speed, consistency, and delivery quality across research workflows that have historically depended on repetitive manual effort and hard-to-scale specialist knowledge. The product surface is unusual. Surveys behave like programs, business workflows contain hidden operational nuance, and a small mistake can create real downstream cost for an agency and its clients. That means product thinking here is not about copying familiar SaaS patterns. It is about understanding how work is actually done, identifying where AI agents can reliably help, and shaping systems that feel intuitive to users while introducing genuinely new workflows underneath. ## The Role You'll be paired with a senior product manager and work closely with senior engineers on a live, shipping product area. Think of this as a structured apprenticeship into product management: you'll take on real pieces of the work — sitting in on user calls, drafting write-ups, helping think through a feature — with a senior PM reviewing, coaching, and gradually handing you more rope as you show you're ready for it. This role is for someone early in their career who is curious, organized, and eager to learn how product decisions actually get made — not someone expected to already operate independently in ambiguity. You'll be given scoped pieces of larger problems, not owning full ambiguity solo. ## What You'll Do - Sit in on user interviews with research operators, project managers, and agency leaders — and take the lead on some, once you're ready — to learn how work actually happens. - Take structured notes and help organize what you hear into clear themes, with a senior PM helping you spot what matters. - Start recognizing the difference between what a user asks for and the real problem underneath, with coaching. - Help write up product ideas, user flows, and simple requirements docs for a senior PM to review and refine. - Take a first pass at breaking a defined problem into smaller, engineering-sized pieces, with guidance. - Help build and test simple prototypes or mockups to get early feedback from users and the team. - Sit in on engineering discussions to learn how requirements turn into shipped software. - Answer engineers' clarifying questions on the pieces of work you own, escalating to your senior PM when you're unsure. - Track the status of the features you're closest to and flag blockers early. - Help gather feedback after something ships — from users, from support tickets, from usage data — and summarize what you find. - Notice when something isn't working as intended and bring it to your senior PM rather than being expected to fix it solo. ## Representative Problems Examples of the kinds of problems you'll get exposure to, usually as part of a larger effort led by a senior PM: - Helping map out how a raw client questionnaire currently becomes a survey, as input to redesigning that workflow. - Sitting in on the design of review and approval loops where human operators check AI agent output. - Documenting how a fragmented project-management flow works today, so a senior PM can redesign it. - Taking notes from conversations with internal subject matter experts and turning them into a simple written summary. ## What We're Looking For ### Must Have - 0-2 years of full-time experience, or strong internship experience, in a business, technical, or analytical role — product management background is a plus but not required. - Strong written communication — you can summarize a conversation or a problem clearly and simply. - Genuine curiosity about how software products get built, and comfort asking questions when you don't understand something. - Comfort talking to people outside your own function (users, engineers, designers) and taking good notes from those conversations. - Basic organizational skills — you can track a few moving pieces of work and follow up without things falling through the cracks. - Coachability — you're looking for regular feedback and want a senior PM actively shaping your growth, not a fully independent role. ### Nice to Have - Some exposure to how software gets built (a technical degree, a coding bootcamp, an engineering internship, or just genuine interest). - Any prior exposure to B2B software, workflow tools, or AI products. - Familiarity with tools like Figma, Notion, or basic SQL — not required, easy to pick up on the job. ## Why Metaforms - A real apprenticeship into product management — close mentorship from senior PMs and senior engineers, not a sink-or-swim first job. - Work on AI products that operate in real production environments, not demos or feature theater. - Join a team where product, engineering, and domain understanding are tightly coupled. - Visible, real work from day one — your notes, write-ups, and small feature areas genuinely shape what gets built. - Join a Series A funded company at the steepest part of its growth curve.
